transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your busy schedule. 

Well, um... I suppose what made me come in is just that my eating has gotten a little bit turned around lately. It's probably nothing, really, maybe just my age catching up with me. But some days I just completely forget to have lunch altogether. And then other days, I'll catch myself just standing at the kitchen counter, picking at crackers and sweets... even though nothing really tastes quite right to me right now. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit I'm not keeping a proper schedule, I know I should be doing better. Does that make sense, doctor? I hope I'm answering your question alright.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticed that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Oh, well... I really try not to complain, doctor. I know everyone gets a little sad sometimes, and I should just be grateful for what I have. But... um... I suppose I have been feeling a little bit down lately. 

It's probably silly, but most mornings I wake up with this... well, this heavy, low feeling. It's almost like the color has just gone out of the day before I even manage to get dressed. I try my best to shake it off, I really do, because I hate being a bother to anyone with my moods. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing.
You mentioned feeling low most mornings and having changes in your eating - how long has this been going on, would you say days, weeks, or longer?

Well, um... I suppose it's been a little while now. I really didn't want to make a big deal out of it, you know? I kept thinking I could just snap out of it on my own, like I should be able to. 

But if I'm being perfectly honest... that low, colorless stretch, the one where the days just feel so heavy... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. I know that sounds like a terribly long time to let something go on without saying anything. I'm so sorry, I probably should have come in sooner. I just didn't want to be a nuisance. 

Is that alright, doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of timeline.
Over this past year and two months, has this low, heavy feeling been present nearly every day without much break, or have there been stretches of weeks where your mood felt normal again?

Well, um... I really hope I'm explaining this properly. I don't want to sound like I'm making things up or being difficult. 

There actually was a little bit of a break... maybe for a few weeks? It was quite nice, really. The heaviness lifted just enough that I was able to eat a bit more regularly, and I felt quite proud of myself for getting dressed properly every day. I thought I was finally getting back to my old self, like I should be. 

But, um... well, even during that better time... I don't know if I should mention this, it sounds so silly... but I still couldn't shake this feeling I've been having. I noticed that the dates and names on some of my records and papers... they just seemed different. Like someone was changing them on purpose, trying to send me a message or signal something to me. 

I know that probably sounds very strange, doctor. I'm sorry if that's not what you were asking about. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
That belief about the dates and names being changed - has that continued on and off up until now, even during times when your mood felt better, or has it gone away completely at some point?

Oh, well... I really hope it's okay to talk about this. I know it sounds so foolish, and I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. I'm sure it's just my imagination getting the better of me. 

But, um... well, to answer your question... those thoughts about the messages in my family records and medical papers... they haven't really gone away. I'd say they started... oh, about a year and a month ago? And they've sort of just stuck around ever since, even when my mood felt a bit lighter. 

I try not to pay too much attention to it, really I do. I just put the papers away and try to focus on my chores. I know I shouldn't let silly things like that bother me. 

Is that... does that answer your question, doctor? I hope I'm not making things too complicated for you.
Have you had any recent medical issues, head injuries, new medications, or use of alcohol or drugs that started around the same time these feelings and beliefs began?

Oh, no, no... nothing like that. I really try to take good care of myself, you know? I haven't had any falls or bumps to the head, thank goodness. And I certainly don't use any... well, any drugs or anything improper like that. Just my usual cup of tea in the afternoon. 

I haven't started any new medicines either, just the same daily vitamins I've always taken. I really try to be a good patient and keep myself healthy so I don't have to bother anyone. 

I hope that's what you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and not taking up too much of your time with things that don't matter.

During that few-week period when you felt better and your mood lifted, did you still find yourself believing the dates and names on your papers were being changed, or did that belief go away completely during that time?

Well, um... yes, I think so. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I know you have so many important things to keep track of. 

But yes, during those few weeks when the heavy feeling lifted—when I was finally eating a bit better and getting dressed like a proper lady should—that... that feeling about the papers was still there. I still felt quite sure that the dates and names in my records were being changed, like someone was trying to signal something to me. 

I know it sounds so silly, and I really did try to just ignore it and focus on my chores so I wouldn't be a bother. But it just didn't go away, even when I was feeling more like myself. 

I hope it's alright that I'm telling you this. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly, doctor. Am I doing okay?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient describes a depressive episode (depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite disturbance) lasting over a year, meeting mood episode criteria. Concurrently, she reports a persistent delusional belief (papers/records being altered to send her signals) that began about a month before the mood episode and persisted unchanged even during a distinct several-week period when her mood normalized. Because psychotic (delusional) symptoms occurred for a significant duration in the absence of a mood episode, this rules out Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which requires psychosis only during mood episodes) and instead supports Schizoaffective Disorder, depressive type. The overall predominance of depressive symptoms over the illness course, absence of manic symptoms, and no substance/medical cause further support F25.1 over F20.9 (Schizophrenia) or F32.3.
